what: Accumulate moderate-intensity aerobic activity (e.g., brisk walking, dancing, cycling) across the week; count every session, including short chunks.
dose: 150-300 min/week moderate OR 75-150 min/week vigorous, or an equivalent combination (WHO 2020; Saudi MOH: at least 150 min moderate or 75 min vigorous, up to 300 min moderate for more benefit). CDC: can be split into smaller chunks, e.g., 30 min x 5 days.
why: WHO states some activity is better than none and more is better; meeting the weekly range provides health benefits for adults.

cue_suggestion: After Asr prayer on your training days; walking fills the other days.
minimum_version: 10 min brisk walk or one dance song block - it still counts toward the weekly total.
normal_version: 30-40 min moderate session (brisk walk or home cardio) on ~4-5 days/week to land in 150-300 min.
bonus_version: Add 1-2 vigorous intervals sessions (e.g., stairs, fast dance) - 1 min vigorous is roughly equal to 2 min moderate in guideline math.
joy_pairing: Pair with a favourite playlist/podcast used only during activity; rotate formats (walk, dance workout, cycling) weekly for novelty.
friction_down: Weekly minutes bar in the app that auto-adds walks and workouts; shoes and mat kept visible; pre-chosen workout video queued the night before.
friction_up_for_competing: Put the phone's entertainment apps behind a 'after movement' shortcut on workout days.
if_then_plan: If it is Asr time on a workout day and I feel low energy, then I will do the 10-minute minimum version instead of skipping.
tracking_metric: Active minutes this week (auto-sum) vs 150 target.
progression: Self-paced: start from current weekly minutes and build toward 150, then toward 300 (sources state the range, not a weekly increase rate).
safety_or_stop_rule: See BODY-25 stop rules. Walk outdoors only in cooler hours during hot weather.

what: Walk daily and track steps with the phone or a watch; raise the daily average gradually from her own baseline.
dose: Dose-response evidence (observational): inflection at around 5,000-7,000 steps/day for all-cause mortality, CVD, dementia and falls; 7,000 vs 2,000 steps/day linked to 47% lower all-cause mortality (Ding 2025). In adults <60, mortality risk kept falling up to 8,000-10,000 steps/day (Paluch 2022). No official step target is set.
why: More daily steps are associated with lower risk of death, heart disease and depressive symptoms, with most of the gain reached by about 7,000 steps/day.

cue_suggestion: After Maghrib prayer (cooler hours) or right after a phone call - 'walk-and-talk'.
minimum_version: 1,000 extra steps: a 10-min walk around the house/mall corridor.
normal_version: Reach ~7,000 steps/day on most days.
bonus_version: 8,000-10,000 steps via a longer evening walk with a friend/family member.
joy_pairing: Walk-and-talk calls with a friend; audiobook or IELTS listening podcast only while walking (temptation bundle); malls or corniche for scenery.
friction_down: Step widget on home screen; default walking route saved; comfortable shoes by the door.
if_then_plan: If by 8 pm I am under 5,000 steps, then I will do a 15-minute indoor walk while listening to my podcast.
progression: Self-paced: raise 7-day average in small steps from baseline; sources give dose-response, not a ramp rate.
safety_or_stop_rule: Avoid outdoor walking in peak heat; carry water; stop per BODY-25.

what: Stand up and move (walk, stairs, a few squats) during long study/desk sessions.
dose: Saudi PHA: reduce prolonged sitting and break it up as often as possible with at least light activity. WHO: reduce sedentary time (no threshold quantified). In crossover trials, interrupting sitting at least every 30 min lowered glucose more than less frequent breaks (Yin 2024).
why: Replacing sitting with any activity carries health benefits, and frequent breaks improved post-meal glucose in lab trials.

cue_suggestion: End of each Pomodoro/study block, or every time a video lesson ends.
normal_version: 2-3 min walk or stairs every ~30 min of sitting.
bonus_version: Take calls and meeting-free reading standing or walking.
joy_pairing: Use the break as a 'song break' - one song, move to it.
friction_down: Timer built into the app's focus sessions; water bottle kept away from the desk so refills force a walk.
if_then_plan: If my focus timer ends, then I will stand and walk until the next song ends.
tracking_metric: Number of breaks taken today (tap per break).
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.

what: Insert 1-2 minute bursts of vigorous effort into daily life: fast stairs, brisk uphill walking, fast squats or jumping jacks.
dose: Observational: ~3 bouts/day of 1-2 min vigorous intermittent lifestyle activity was associated with 38-40% lower all-cause mortality in non-exercisers (UK Biobank, mean age ~62). Low-certainty SR: exercise snacks give a small improvement in neuromuscular performance in insufficiently active adults. No official dose.
why: Brief vigorous bursts are associated with lower mortality and can be a starting point for people not doing structured exercise.

cue_suggestion: Every time she takes the stairs or before sitting down to study.
normal_version: 3 bursts across the day.
bonus_version: Use on rest-from-workout days to keep momentum.
joy_pairing: Treat it as a game: 'beat the song chorus' burst; streak confetti in the app.
friction_down: No equipment, no changing clothes needed.
friction_up_for_competing: Choose stairs over elevator as a default rule.
if_then_plan: If I arrive at a building with stairs, then I will take them fast for the first flights.
safety_or_stop_rule: Vigorous effort: stop per BODY-25 warning signs.

what: Train all major muscle groups (legs, hips, back, abdomen, chest, shoulders, arms) at home with bodyweight, bands or dumbbells; progress when the current load becomes easy.
dose: At least 2 days/week for all major muscle groups (WHO, CDC, Saudi MOH); ACSM: 2-3 days/week. Observational dose-response: maximum risk reduction at ~30-60 min/week of muscle-strengthening (Momma 2022). Novices: loads around 8-12 repetition maximum, 2-3 days/week; increase load 2-10% when she can do 1-2 reps more than target (ACSM 2009).
why: Muscle-strengthening activity is associated with 10-17% lower risk of all-cause mortality, CVD, cancer and diabetes, independent of aerobic activity.

cue_suggestion: After Asr prayer on 2-3 of your training days.
minimum_version: One circuit: squat, push-up (wall/knee), glute bridge, row with band - 1 set each.
normal_version: 20-30 min full-body session, 1-3 sets per exercise, reps in the 8-12 range to near-fatigue.
bonus_version: Add a third weekly session or a harder variation (split squat, elevated push-up).
joy_pairing: Upbeat playlist (BODY-11); 'new move of the week' for novelty; log a PR badge when a harder variation is unlocked.
friction_down: Mat and bands stay out; one saved routine with video demos; no decision needed on the day.
friction_up_for_competing: Workout starts before phone social time after Asr.
if_then_plan: If I can do 2 reps more than my target on an exercise for two sessions, then I will move to the next harder variation or heavier weight.
tracking_metric: Sessions this week (0-3) + top variation/weight per exercise.
progression: ACSM 2009: increase load 2-10% when current load allows 1-2 reps above target. For bodyweight, a harder variation is the home equivalent (adaptation, not stated in source).
safety_or_stop_rule: Controlled form; sharp joint pain = stop that exercise. See BODY-25.

what: Stretch each major muscle-tendon group; end workouts or study days with a short mobility routine.
dose: ACSM 2011: flexibility exercises for each major muscle-tendon group, a total of 60 s per exercise, on at least 2 days/week. Strength training itself also improves joint flexibility (SR, high risk of bias).
why: Flexibility exercise maintains joint range of motion (ACSM).

cue_suggestion: Immediately after a strength session, or after Isha before wind-down.
normal_version: 8-10 min covering the major groups, 60 s total each.
bonus_version: Guided mobility/yoga-style video on a rest day.
joy_pairing: Calm playlist, dim warm light - doubles as a wind-down cue (BODY-17).
friction_down: One saved 10-min routine; do it on the same mat.
if_then_plan: If I finish a workout, then I will do my 60-second stretches before showering.
safety_or_stop_rule: Stretch to mild tension, not pain.

what: Optional weekly Pilates-based session (online is fine) as an enjoyable variation within the strength/mobility plan.
dose: not specified by source (SR: even once-weekly programs were associated with improvements, but optimal dose unclear).
why: Pilates-based exercise showed benefits for quality of life and self-esteem; evidence for depression/anxiety is limited; remote and in-person delivery performed similarly in adults.

cue_suggestion: Weekend morning slot.
normal_version: 30-45 min class, once a week.
bonus_version: Do it with a friend over video call.
joy_pairing: Try different instructors for novelty; it counts as a 'fun' workout day.
friction_down: Save 3 favourite videos in the app.
if_then_plan: If I feel bored of my strength routine, then I will swap one session for Pilates that week.
safety_or_stop_rule: Stop if back pain worsens; see professional if persistent.

what: Set up a comfortable laptop/desk arrangement and, more importantly, change position and take brief breaks.
dose: not specified by source. Cochrane: workstation adjustment and sit-stand desks showed no effect on upper-limb pain; supplementary breaks had very-low-quality evidence of reducing neck/shoulder/arm discomfort.
why: Ergonomic equipment alone has weak/inconsistent evidence; breaks have some (very low quality) evidence for less discomfort.

cue_suggestion: Same focus-timer cue as BODY-03.
minimum_version: Change posture and roll shoulders at each timer.
normal_version: Comfortable setup (screen roughly at eye level, feet supported) + BODY-03 breaks.
bonus_version: Laptop stand + external keyboard for long design sessions (comfort choice, not evidence-proven).
joy_pairing: Make the desk a pleasant space (plant, light) she wants to sit at - and leave regularly.
friction_down: One-time setup task in the app.
if_then_plan: If I notice neck or wrist discomfort, then I will stand up and take a 2-minute break immediately.
safety_or_stop_rule: Persistent pain, numbness or tingling: see a physiotherapist/doctor.

what: Pick an intensity that feels good during the session (can talk, feels pleasant) and allow herself to adjust it mid-workout.
dose: not specified by source.
why: Feeling better during moderate exercise predicts future activity; in an RCT, pleasure-oriented intensity prescription led to 77% more gym sessions over 8 weeks; allowing intensity adjustment improved affect in young adults.

cue_suggestion: Start of every workout: rate 'how do I feel?' on a -5..+5 scale.
minimum_version: Keep the session but lower intensity if the feeling drops below 0.
normal_version: Stay in the zone that feels pleasant most of the time.
bonus_version: Push harder only at the end when feeling good (end on a high).
joy_pairing: End each session with the favourite move/song so the remembered feeling is positive.
friction_down: One-tap feeling rating in the app before/after.
if_then_plan: If the workout starts feeling bad, then I will lower the intensity rather than stop.
safety_or_stop_rule: See BODY-25.

what: Listen to music she likes during exercise; faster-tempo tracks for cardio/strength.
dose: not specified by source.
why: Meta-analysis of 139 studies: music improved affective valence, physical performance, and reduced perceived exertion; performance effects larger with fast tempo.

cue_suggestion: Pressing play = workout starts.
normal_version: Dedicated workout playlist for the whole session.
bonus_version: Build playlists by tempo for warm-up, main set, cool-down.
joy_pairing: Workout-only playlist she looks forward to.
friction_down: Playlist linked from the workout card in the app.
if_then_plan: If I don't feel like exercising, then I will put on my workout playlist and only commit to the first song.
tracking_metric: None needed (optional: favourite track of the week).
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep volume safe; stay aware of surroundings when walking outdoors.

what: Reserve a 'want' pleasure (a gripping audiobook, series, podcast) for exercise time only.
dose: not specified by source.
why: In a field experiment, gym-only access to tempting audiobooks increased gym visits by 51% initially, though effects declined over time (especially after a holiday).

cue_suggestion: Walking or cardio sessions.

joy_pairing: This IS the joy pairing.
friction_down: Downloaded episodes ready offline.
friction_up_for_competing: Hide the bundled app/series from the home screen outside workout time.
if_then_plan: If I want to hear the next chapter, then I will put on my shoes and walk.
safety_or_stop_rule: Stay alert to traffic if walking outdoors.

dose: not specified by source.

cue_suggestion: App detects a missed planned workout.

bonus_version: Two comebacks in a row unlock something she wants (new playlist, class).

friction_down: Auto-reschedule missed session to the next free slot.
if_then_plan: If I miss a planned workout, then I will do the minimum version at the next Asr and log a comeback.
safety_or_stop_rule: If missed due to illness, rest first (BODY-25).

what: Schedule some walks/workouts with a friend, sister, or an online class/group; or set up mutual check-ins.
dose: not specified by source.

if_then_plan: If my buddy cancels, then I will do the walk alone with my bundled podcast.
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.

dose: Adults: 7 or more hours per night (AASM/SRS; CDC for ages 18-60; Saudi PHA: >=7 h of good sleep, young adults 18-25 aim for 7-9 h).
why: Consensus statements define >=7 h as the amount needed to promote optimal health in adults.

dose: Meta-analysis: coffee (~107 mg/250 mL) at least 8.8 h before bedtime; a standard pre-workout supplement (~217.5 mg) at least 13.2 h before bedtime. CDC: avoid caffeine in the afternoon or evening.
why: Caffeine reduced total sleep time by 45 min and sleep efficiency by 7% on average.

safety_or_stop_rule: None.

what: Get bright light during the day, ideally daylight (e.g., sit by a window while studying, short outdoor time in cooler early hours).
dose: Expert consensus: daytime minimum melanopic EDI of 250 lux at the eye; use daylight first where available. No minutes-per-day dose stated.
why: Consensus recommends bright daytime light to support circadian rhythm, sleep and alertness.

bonus_version: Morning walk outdoors when temperature allows (combine with BODY-02).

if_then_plan: If I start a study session, then I will sit in the brightest daylit spot available.

what: Decide a 'go to bed' time and pre-commit with a plan for the usual delay trigger (scrolling, series, late work).
dose: not specified by source.

cue_suggestion: Wind-down alarm (BODY-17).

bonus_version: Move 'revenge' leisure (series) to earlier evening as a planned reward.
joy_pairing: Schedule guilt-free leisure earlier so bedtime doesn't feel like losing 'me time'.
friction_down: Auto Do Not Disturb + app lock at wind-down.
friction_up_for_competing: Log out of the most tempting app at night; disable autoplay.
if_then_plan: If one episode ends after my wind-down time, then I will close the app and not start the next.
safety_or_stop_rule: None.

what: If sleepy, take a short nap around midday; keep it short.
dose: Saudi PHA: napping around midday (noontime) is acceptable, limited to less than 30 min. Cohort meta-analysis: naps >=30 min associated with higher mortality/CVD/metabolic risk; <30 min not. Lab meta-analysis: naps improved alertness, with early-afternoon naps (before 13:00) better.
why: Short naps improved cognitive performance (especially alertness) in lab studies, while long habitual naps were associated with higher health risks.

what: Keep the bedroom quiet, cool and dark; avoid large meals before bedtime.

cue_suggestion: One-time setup + weekly check on the weekend.

friction_up_for_competing: Keep work laptop off the bed.
if_then_plan: If dinner is late, then I will keep it light.
safety_or_stop_rule: None.

dose: Saudi PHA (as extracted from guideline PDF): sufficient sleep of 4-6 h at night supplemented by 1.5-2 h daytime sleep.
why: Saudi consensus recognizes Ramadan's changed schedule and recommends maintaining adequate total sleep.

dose: NHS: aim for 6-8 cups or glasses of fluid a day (water, lower-fat milk, sugar-free drinks including tea and coffee count); more if in a hot environment or physically active for long periods. EFSA: 2.0 L/day considered adequate for women (total water intake).
why: Official bodies set adequate intakes; needs rise in hot environments and with prolonged activity.

what: Limit added sugars and sweets (desserts, sweetened snacks, honey/syrups, juices) to planned, enjoyable portions.

why: WHO recommends limiting salt intake as part of a healthy diet (salt reduction lowers blood pressure risk).

cue_suggestion: When planning the cooking method for dinner.

name_en: Protein spread across the day (training days)

why: Protein intake plus resistance exercise enhances gains in muscle strength and size in healthy adults.

cue_suggestion: When plating each main meal: 'where's the protein?'.

cue_suggestion: The moment a study timer ends (before standing up)

if_then_plan: If my study timer rings, then I close the book and write everything I remember before checking.

what: Instead of cramming, schedule each topic to come back for review on later days; the further away the exam/need, the longer the gap between reviews. Reviews are done as retrieval (GROW-01).

why: Distributing study over time improves long-term retention compared with massed study; distributed practice was rated high utility.

cue_suggestion: Sunday evening weekly planning (app schedules reviews automatically)

friction_down: Use a spaced-repetition app/deck so the schedule is automatic; app shows 'due today' count.
friction_up_for_competing: Don't allow 'new lesson' to start until due reviews are cleared.
if_then_plan: If I open my study app, then I clear due reviews before starting anything new.
progression: Gaps lengthen as the target date moves further away (Cepeda 2008 ratio); otherwise self-paced

what: When practising categories that are easy to confuse (e.g., IELTS Writing Task 1 chart types, Reading question types, UI patterns/heuristic violations), mix them in one session instead of doing all of one type, then all of the next.
dose: not specified by source - start by mixing 2-3 types per session
why: Interleaving had a moderate overall benefit for inductive learning, strongest for visual material and categories that look similar to each other.

cue_suggestion: When building a practice set for the week
minimum_version: Do 3 mixed questions of different types.
normal_version: A practice set that shuffles 3-4 question types.

friction_down: Use shuffled/mixed practice sets rather than chapter-by-chapter exercises.

what: While studying an example (a model IELTS essay, a worked case study, a solved problem), stop after each step and answer: 'Why is this done? How does it connect to what I know?' - out loud or in a margin note.

what: Read easy-to-comfortable English material you enjoy (articles, blogs in your field, graded readers, novels) for meaning, not for testing - aim for flow, not dictionary lookups.

cue_suggestion: After Isha / before bed wind-down (paper or e-ink rather than phone)

cue_suggestion: After Fajr/morning routine for block 1; after Dhuhr for block 2
normal_version: 2 blocks of ~45 min with a 5-10 min movement break between.
bonus_version: A third block on low-demand work (admin, tracker updates).
joy_pairing: Signature focus soundtrack + favourite drink + a 'done' ritual (tick in app).
friction_down: Block and its single task pre-written the night before; materials open.
friction_up_for_competing: Phone in another room; website blocker on during blocks.
if_then_plan: If I start a focus block, then I put my phone in the other room first.
safety_or_stop_rule: Take breaks to move and rest eyes; don't stretch blocks at the expense of sleep.

name_en: If-then plan for the day's top task (anti-procrastination)
what: Each evening, choose tomorrow's single most important task and write an if-then plan: 'If [time/place], then I will [first 2-minute step]'. When avoiding a task, shrink it to the first physical step.
dose: not specified by source
why: Implementation intentions had a medium-to-large effect on goal attainment (d = .65) across 94 tests, helping to start tasks and shield them from distraction; procrastination interventions produced large reductions overall.

sources.title: Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes
Overcoming procrastination? A meta-analysis of intervention studies

cue_suggestion: Evening wind-down, after Isha
normal_version: Top task + if-then plan + first 2-minute step.
bonus_version: Add one if-then for the most likely obstacle ('If I feel like scrolling, then I open the doc and write one line').
joy_pairing: Let tomorrow-self start with a small win; pair the first step with a favourite morning drink.
friction_down: App prompt at the evening slot with the template pre-filled.
if_then_plan: If it's after Isha, then I write tomorrow's top task and its if-then plan in the app.
safety_or_stop_rule: Chronic procrastination with distress: CBT-based approaches reduced procrastination most in the meta-analysis - that is a professional's domain; seek support if it seriously affects studies/work.

what: Set app time limits for the social apps she uses most, rather than quitting completely; run it as a 3-week experiment and compare mood/focus before and after.
dose: Source-stated trial doses: Hunt 2018 limited Facebook/Instagram/Snapchat to 10 min per platform per day (~30 min/day total) for 3 weeks; Thrul 2025 reanalysis: reductions/abstinence of 1 week or longer showed small benefits, shorter than 1 week showed small harms, with ~3 weeks suggested as possibly ideal (unconfirmed).
why: Limiting social media reduced loneliness and depression in undergraduates, and deactivating Facebook for 4 weeks increased subjective wellbeing - but overall experimental evidence is mixed and effects are small.

sources.title: No More FOMO: Limiting Social Media Decreases Loneliness and Depression
The Welfare Effects of Social Media
Do social media experiments prove a link with mental health: A methodological and meta-analytic review
Social Media Reduction or Abstinence Interventions Are Providing Mental Health Benefits - Reanalysis of a Published Meta-Analysis
Digital detox: An effective solution in the smartphone era? A systematic literature review

cue_suggestion: Set once; weekly check in the Thursday review
minimum_version: One app with a daily time limit.
normal_version: App limits on main social apps (e.g., ~10 min each) for 3 weeks.
bonus_version: Move social apps off the home screen / log out on phone, use only on laptop.
joy_pairing: Replace scrolling slots with a pleasant alternative she picks (reading, walk podcast, calling a friend).
friction_down: Use built-in Screen Time / Digital Wellbeing limits.
friction_up_for_competing: Log out after each use; delete apps from phone (keep web version).
if_then_plan: If my social media limit is reached, then I close the app and open my reading/podcast instead.
tracking_metric: Minutes on social apps today (auto from phone)
progression: Hold for at least 1 week (ideally ~3) before judging; self-paced after
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep channels needed for work/portfolio/job search (e.g., LinkedIn in scheduled blocks). Short full-abstinence stints (<1 week) may feel worse.

what: Run a 3-week experiment capping recreational smartphone screen time, or blocking mobile internet for set periods while keeping calls/texts; use the freed time for in-person time, exercise and outdoors. Measure wellbeing, sleep and focus before/after.
dose: Source-stated trial doses: Pieh 2025 - screen time reduced to <=2 h/day for 3 weeks in healthy students; Castelo 2025 - mobile internet blocked for 2 weeks (calls/texts and desktop internet kept).
why: Cutting smartphone screen time to <=2 h/day for 3 weeks improved wellbeing, depressive symptoms, sleep quality and stress in students; blocking mobile internet for 2 weeks improved sustained attention, mental health and wellbeing, partly via more socialising, exercise and time in nature.

sources.title: Smartphone screen time reduction improves mental health: a randomized controlled trial
Blocking mobile internet on smartphones improves sustained attention, mental health, and subjective well-being
Digital detox: An effective solution in the smartphone era? A systematic literature review

cue_suggestion: Start on a Sunday; weekly check in the Thursday review
minimum_version: Phone-free first 30 min after waking or last 30 min before sleep.
normal_version: Daily recreational screen-time cap (e.g., <=2 h as in Pieh) for 3 weeks, tracked automatically.
bonus_version: Mobile data off during chosen hours (keep calls/texts) for 2 weeks.
joy_pairing: Pre-plan what replaces screen time: walks, driving practice, reading, family/friends - make the 'offline list' fun.
friction_down: Built-in screen-time limits; laptop for necessary internet work.
friction_up_for_competing: Grey out/limit video apps; charger outside the bedroom.
if_then_plan: If I reach my daily screen-time limit, then I pick an activity from my offline list.
tracking_metric: Daily screen time (auto) + weekly WHO-5-style mood check (self-rated)
progression: 3-week block (as tested), then keep what worked; self-paced
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep phone access for safety, family and navigation (especially while learning to drive). If mood problems persist, see a professional.

name_en: Confirm the official licence path and enrol in a driving school
name_ar: تأكيد خطوات الرخصة الرسمية والتسجيل في مدرسة القيادة
what: Open Absher / my.gov.sa (service: 'Driving license issuance') and the chosen driving school's official page; write down, in the app, the current steps, prerequisites (e.g., medical check, fees, eye test), the course level assigned, and test dates. Then book the school.
dose: not specified by source (official pages could not be read from the research environment; confirm hours and steps directly on Absher/my.gov.sa and with the school)
why: The official process and required training hours are set by the traffic authority and schools and can change; planning must follow the current official version.
cue_suggestion: Sunday life-admin block
minimum_version: Open the my.gov.sa service page and save the link in the app.
normal_version: Fill a one-page checklist of steps, documents, fees and dates, then book the school's assessment.
bonus_version: Call/WhatsApp the school to confirm course hours for your assessed level and the earliest test slot.
joy_pairing: Treat it as a milestone: each checklist item done unlocks a small reward (favourite drink, a playlist for future drives).
friction_down: Keep national ID, photos and payment method ready in one folder; pre-fill Absher login with 2-step verification enabled.
friction_up_for_competing: Do not open social media until the checklist is filled.
if_then_plan: If it is Sunday life-admin time, then I will open the licence checklist and complete the next unchecked step.
safety_or_stop_rule: Use only official government portals and licensed driving schools; ignore third-party 'fast licence' offers.

name_ar: تدريب نشط على إدراك مخاطر الطريق
what: Practise spotting developing hazards using active (respond/predict) exercises: hazard-perception video clips where you click or say the hazard before it happens, 'what happens next' prediction, and commentary driving with the instructor.
dose: not specified by source (meta-analysis: active training and even single sessions gave consistent short-term gains; long-term retention unclear)
why: Hazard perception training produced a large improvement in drivers' hazard-perception skill (g = 0.78), with active training most consistent.

sources.title: The efficacy of hazard perception training and education: A systematic review and meta-analysis
The effectiveness of mandating supervised driving practice requirements on improving road safety outcomes for learner drivers: A systematic review

cue_suggestion: Right after a driving lesson, or the evening before one
minimum_version: Watch 1 hazard clip and name the hazard out loud before it appears.
normal_version: One short active hazard-perception session (clips + prediction) and write 1 hazard you missed in the lesson.
bonus_version: Commentary drive with the instructor: narrate hazards aloud for part of the lesson.
joy_pairing: Make it a game: score your clip reactions and try to beat yesterday's score; do it with a friend/sister who is also learning.
friction_down: Save a playlist of hazard clips (from the driving school or theory app) on the phone home screen.
friction_up_for_competing: Use it as the 'unlock' before evening scrolling.
if_then_plan: If I finish a driving lesson, then I will spend a few minutes on hazard clips and log one hazard I missed.
progression: self-paced; move from clips to commentary driving as the instructor allows
safety_or_stop_rule: Never watch clips or use the phone while driving.

name_en: Build supervised practice across varied conditions
name_ar: تراكم ساعات تدريب تحت الإشراف في ظروف متنوعة
what: After the course, keep accumulating supervised practice (instructor, or as permitted by Saudi traffic rules) and deliberately widen exposure step by step: quiet streets, then busier roads, night, highways, parking, your city's traffic peaks.
dose: not specified by source (review: more supervised practice associated with safer outcomes, but specific hour thresholds were mixed)
why: Longer learner periods, structured training and greater supervised practice were associated with fewer crashes and offences in early independent driving.

sources.title: The effectiveness of mandating supervised driving practice requirements on improving road safety outcomes for learner drivers: A systematic review

cue_suggestion: Fixed weekly slot (e.g., Friday after Asr) with the supervising person
minimum_version: 10 minutes in a quiet familiar area practising one manoeuvre.
normal_version: One planned practice drive on a pre-chosen route targeting one new condition.
bonus_version: Add a new condition (night/highway) once the current one feels routine.
joy_pairing: Pair with a pleasant destination (favourite café drive-through) and a 'driving playlist' at low volume once confident.
friction_down: Plan the route in the app beforehand; keep a 'conditions ladder' checklist.
if_then_plan: If it is Friday after Asr and the supervisor is free, then I will drive the planned route for today's condition.
tracking_metric: Practice minutes + condition ticked on the ladder
progression: Advance one rung on the conditions ladder only when the previous feels routine (self-paced)
safety_or_stop_rule: Only drive when legally permitted (licence or valid permit with required supervision); stop if very anxious, tired, or in bad visibility (dust/rain).

name_en: Spaced practice tests for the theory exam
what: Prepare the theory test (signs, rules) with short practice-test sessions spread over days instead of one long cram.
dose: not specified by source
why: Practice testing and distributed practice were rated the highest-utility learning techniques in a major review.

sources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology

cue_suggestion: After Isha, before any leisure screen time
normal_version: One practice set and review every wrong answer.
bonus_version: Full mock test under time.
joy_pairing: Track a streak and a rising score chart; do it with tea in a favourite spot.
friction_down: Use the official/school practice material saved on the home screen.
if_then_plan: If I finish Isha, then I will do one short theory practice set before opening social apps.
progression: self-paced; stop when consistently passing mock tests
safety_or_stop_rule: Use only official/school-provided question banks for content accuracy.

name_en: Track spending for a week, then make a monthly spending plan
name_ar: تتبع المصروفات أسبوعًا ثم خطة صرف شهرية
what: List income sources, track every spend by category for one week, list bills with due dates, then write a simple monthly spending plan; review weekly and update when income or habits change.
dose: Tracking 'one week at a time' is suggested by CFPB; review frequency otherwise not specified by source
why: CFPB's consumer guidance uses income tracker, spending tracker and bill calendar as the steps to build and keep a working budget.

sources.title: CFPB - Budgeting: How to create a budget and stick with it

cue_suggestion: Right after a purchase (log) and on payday (plan)
minimum_version: Log today's spends with one tap each.
normal_version: Weekly 10-minute review of categories vs plan.
bonus_version: Monthly: adjust categories and move any surplus to a goal.
joy_pairing: Visual progress bars per goal; reward a 'good week' with a small planned treat that is inside the budget.
friction_down: Use bank notifications or a one-tap logger; pre-set categories.
friction_up_for_competing: Remove saved cards from impulse-shopping apps.
if_then_plan: If I pay for something, then I will log it before leaving the shop/app.
safety_or_stop_rule: If debts or money stress feel unmanageable, seek help from the bank or a qualified adviser.

name_en: Automatic transfer to savings on payday
what: Set a recurring bank transfer from current to savings account scheduled on payday (pay-yourself-first default).
dose: Amount not specified by source; start small and adjust
why: Defaults strongly shape saving: automatic enrolment raised retirement-plan participation, and defaults show a considerable average effect in meta-analysis (d = 0.68).

sources.title: CFPB - An essential guide to building an emergency fund
The Power of Suggestion: Inertia in 401(k) Participation and Savings Behavior
When and why defaults influence decisions: a meta-analysis of default effects
The effectiveness of nudging: A meta-analysis of choice architecture interventions across behavioral domains

cue_suggestion: Payday (automated)
normal_version: A set percentage of income that fits the plan.
bonus_version: Raise the amount a little after each pay rise or windfall.
joy_pairing: Name the account after the dream (e.g., 'My car', 'Trip') and watch the balance grow.
friction_down: Automate once; no monthly decision needed.
friction_up_for_competing: Keep savings in a separate account without a debit card.
if_then_plan: If I receive a raise or gift money, then I will increase the automatic transfer that day.
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep enough in current account for bills to avoid overdraft or late fees.

name_en: Build an emergency fund in a separate account
what: Keep a dedicated cash reserve for unplanned expenses; size the target from the kinds and costs of unexpected expenses you've had; add windfalls (gifts, bonuses) and monitor the running total.
dose: Target not specified by source ('depends on your situation'); even a small amount helps
why: CFPB: an emergency fund provides a cash reserve for unplanned expenses; even a small amount gives some financial security.

sources.title: CFPB - An essential guide to building an emergency fund

cue_suggestion: Payday + whenever a gift/bonus arrives
minimum_version: Start the account with any amount.
normal_version: Automatic monthly top-up until the chosen target.
bonus_version: Save part of every windfall.
joy_pairing: Progress ring toward the target; celebrate milestones (25/50/75/100%).
friction_down: Separate account, auto transfer, balance notifications.
friction_up_for_competing: No card linked to this account.
if_then_plan: If I get gift/bonus money, then I will move part of it to the emergency fund the same day.
safety_or_stop_rule: Use only for true emergencies; refill after use.

what: Give each saving goal its own named pot/sub-account with a visual reminder (e.g., photo of the goal); optionally split one goal into two pots, and optionally lock a goal pot until a date/amount.
dose: not specified by source
why: In a field experiment, partitioning earmarked money into two accounts and adding a visual reminder of the goal increased saving; a commitment (locked) savings product also increased saving in an RCT.

sources.title: Earmarking and Partitioning: Increasing Saving by Low-Income Households
Tying Odysseus to the Mast: Evidence From a Commitment Savings Product in the Philippines
CFPB - An essential guide to building an emergency fund

cue_suggestion: Monthly money review
minimum_version: Rename one savings pot with its goal.
normal_version: One pot per goal with a picture and target date.
bonus_version: Lock one pot until its date if your bank offers it.
joy_pairing: Use a photo of the goal (car, course, trip) as the pot's cover.
friction_down: Most Saudi banking apps allow multiple savings pots/accounts.
if_then_plan: If I feel like dipping into a goal pot, then I will first look at the goal picture and wait one day.
safety_or_stop_rule: Don't lock money you may need for emergencies (keep LIFE-07 first).

name_ar: قواعد شخصية للشراء الآن والدفع لاحقًا
what: Use BNPL only for planned, budgeted purchases; keep at most one active plan at a time; add every instalment date to the bill calendar; check the total still fits the plan before confirming.
dose: Personal rule; limits not specified by source
why: CFPB found BNPL risks of loan stacking across lenders, late fees (10.5% of users charged at least one in 2021) and weaker dispute protections; in Saudi Arabia BNPL companies are regulated by SAMA.

sources.title: CFPB Study Details the Rapid Growth of Buy Now, Pay Later Lending (2022)
SAMA Rulebook - Rules for Regulating Buy-Now-Pay-Later (BNPL) Companies (page existence only; rule text not readable)

cue_suggestion: At checkout when BNPL is offered
minimum_version: Pause 10 seconds and ask: is this in my plan?
normal_version: Check active BNPL plans in the app before accepting a new one.
bonus_version: Pay in full instead when possible.
joy_pairing: Every BNPL skipped = the same amount moved to a goal pot (see progress grow).
friction_down: Keep a single 'Instalments' list with due dates and auto-pay from salary account.
friction_up_for_competing: Turn off BNPL one-click/saved accounts in shopping apps.
if_then_plan: If a checkout offers 'split in 4', then I will check my instalments list before accepting.
safety_or_stop_rule: If instalments start overlapping or a payment is missed, stop new BNPL and contact the provider.

what: Keep a bill calendar of all recurring charges (subscriptions, phone, instalments) and once a month cancel or downgrade anything unused.
dose: Bill calendar per CFPB; monthly review cadence is a practical choice (not specified by source)
why: Knowing what bills are due and when helps spot timing mismatches and keep the budget accurate.

sources.title: CFPB - Budgeting: How to create a budget and stick with it

cue_suggestion: First weekend of the month
minimum_version: Check the list of subscriptions in the phone's app store settings.
normal_version: Review bank statement recurring charges and cancel one unused.
bonus_version: Negotiate or switch a plan (mobile/internet).
joy_pairing: Move saved money straight to a fun goal pot.
friction_down: Keep the bill calendar in the app with reminders 3 days before each due date.
friction_up_for_competing: Use calendar reminders before free trials convert.
if_then_plan: If I start a free trial, then I will set a reminder 2 days before it ends.

name_ar: قائمة أمنيات وفترة تهدئة قبل الشراء غير الضروري
what: Put non-essential items on a wishlist with the date added; buy only if still wanted after a waiting period and it fits the plan.
dose: Waiting period not specified by any verified source; choose one (e.g., a few days) and adjust
why: Practical self-control strategy; no verified trial evidence found for personal cooling-off periods.
cue_suggestion: When you feel the urge to buy online
minimum_version: Add to wishlist instead of cart.
normal_version: Review the wishlist weekly; buy at most the top item if in budget.
bonus_version: Delete items you no longer want and log the 'saved' amount.
joy_pairing: Browsing the wishlist is allowed and fun; celebrate 'saved' totals.
friction_down: Wishlist widget in the app.
friction_up_for_competing: Log out of shopping apps; remove saved cards.
if_then_plan: If I want to buy something not in my plan, then I will add it to the wishlist and decide at the weekly review.
tracking_metric: Items bought vs removed from wishlist

name_en: Just-in-time money learning before big decisions
name_ar: تعلم مالي في وقته قبل القرارات الكبيرة
what: Before a specific decision (car purchase/financing, first job salary account, savings product), spend a focused session learning exactly that topic from official sources, then act soon after.
dose: not specified by source
why: Meta-analyses show financial education effects are real but modest and decay over time, supporting learning tied to an imminent behaviour.

sources.title: Financial Literacy, Financial Education, and Downstream Financial Behaviors
Financial education affects financial knowledge and downstream behaviors

cue_suggestion: When a money decision is added to the calendar
minimum_version: Read one official page on the decision.
normal_version: One session comparing options and total cost, then decide within the week.
bonus_version: Ask a knowledgeable family member to review.
joy_pairing: Treat it as a research mini-project (research mindset).
friction_down: Keep a list of trusted official sources (SAMA, bank product pages).
if_then_plan: If I schedule a big purchase, then I will book a 30-minute research session in the 3 days before.
safety_or_stop_rule: Don't rely on social-media 'finance tips' for regulated products.

what: A short daily reset: clear surfaces, return items to their homes, put clothes in the hamper, set up tomorrow's items.
dose: not specified by source; 10 minutes is a planning estimate
why: Observational studies link homes described as cluttered with worse mood and flatter cortisol slopes in women, and clutter with lower subjective well-being; causality is not established.

sources.title: No place like home: home tours correlate with daily patterns of mood and cortisol
The dark side of home: Assessing possession 'clutter' on subjective well-being

cue_suggestion: Right after Isha prayer, or before the night skincare routine
normal_version: 10-minute timer reset of the whole room.
bonus_version: Prepare tomorrow's outfit and bag.
joy_pairing: One favourite song or podcast episode = the reset; light a scent/incense after.
friction_down: Hamper and a 'drop tray' near the door; fewer items on surfaces.
friction_up_for_competing: Phone charges outside the room until the reset is done.
if_then_plan: If I finish Isha, then I will start the 10-minute reset timer.

name_en: A home for everything: one zone per week
name_ar: مكان لكل شيء: منطقة واحدة أسبوعيًا
what: Declutter and organise one zone per week (desk, wardrobe shelf, makeup, cables), giving every kept item a labelled home; remove/donate what isn't used.
dose: not specified by source
why: Practical, low-risk; supports the daily reset. Evidence linking clutter to wellbeing is observational only.

sources.title: No place like home: home tours correlate with daily patterns of mood and cortisol

cue_suggestion: Saturday morning after breakfast
normal_version: One zone in about 30 minutes.
bonus_version: Donate bag delivered the same week.
joy_pairing: Before/after photos (a mini design case study); music.
friction_down: Keep bins, labels and a donate bag ready.
if_then_plan: If it is Saturday after breakfast, then I will pick this week's zone from the list and set a 30-minute timer.

name_en: Batch laundry on a fixed day
what: Do laundry in batches on fixed day(s): wash, dry, fold and put away in the same session.
dose: not specified by source
why: Practical: batching and a stable cue reduce decisions and pile-ups; no direct evidence.
cue_suggestion: Same weekday each week
normal_version: Wash, fold and put away one full batch.
bonus_version: Iron/prepare the week's outfits.
joy_pairing: Fold while watching a favourite series episode.
friction_down: Separate hampers by colour so sorting is done already.
if_then_plan: If it is laundry day, then I will start the first load before breakfast.

name_en: Weekly life-admin block with errand batching
name_ar: وقت أسبوعي للمهام الإدارية وتجميع المشاوير
what: One fixed weekly block to process the admin inbox: payments, forms, bookings, calls; group errands by location into one trip.
dose: not specified by source
why: Planning when and where to act (implementation intentions) improves remembering and following through on intended tasks.

sources.title: The effect of implementation intention on prospective memory: a systematic and meta-analytic review
Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes

cue_suggestion: Sunday after Asr
minimum_version: Clear 2 items from the admin inbox.
normal_version: Process the whole admin list and plan errands by area.
bonus_version: Pre-book next week's appointments.
joy_pairing: Favourite drink + a tidy desk; tick-off animation in the app.
friction_down: Capture every admin task into one inbox list the moment it appears.
friction_up_for_competing: Do Not Disturb during the block.
if_then_plan: If it is Sunday after Asr, then I will open the admin inbox and start with the oldest item.

what: Keep one register of documents and expiry dates (national ID, passport, driving licence once issued, car registration/insurance, bank cards, subscriptions) and appointments, each with calendar/phone reminders ahead of the date.
dose: Reminder lead time not specified by source
why: Text-message reminders increased attendance at appointments vs no reminders (moderate-quality evidence), and offloading intentions to external reminders reduces memory demand.

sources.title: Mobile phone messaging reminders for attendance at healthcare appointments (Cochrane)
Cognitive Offloading

cue_suggestion: When any document or appointment is created
minimum_version: Add one expiry date with a reminder.
normal_version: Register complete; review monthly.
bonus_version: Scanned copies stored in encrypted backup (see LIFE-19).
joy_pairing: Satisfying 'all green' status screen.
friction_down: Use the app's template fields; double reminders (early + near date).
if_then_plan: If I get a new document or booking, then I will add it to the register before putting it away.
safety_or_stop_rule: Don't store ID numbers in unencrypted notes; renew via official portals only.

name_en: If-then plan for every one-off task
name_ar: خطة (إذا... فسأ...) لكل مهمة لمرة واحدة
what: When adding a one-off task, attach a specific cue: 'If [time/place/event], then I will [action]'. Imagining the moment strengthens it.
dose: not specified by source
why: Implementation intentions improved prospective memory in healthy young adults (d = 0.445), more with verbal + imagery form (d = 0.59).

sources.title: The effect of implementation intention on prospective memory: a systematic and meta-analytic review
Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes

cue_suggestion: At task capture
minimum_version: Add a time or place to the task.
normal_version: Write the full if-then and picture the moment for a few seconds.
bonus_version: Link it to an existing routine step.
joy_pairing: Quick-add templates make it feel effortless.
friction_down: App prompt field 'When/where will you do this?'.
if_then_plan: If I add a task without a cue, then I will add the 'if' part before saving.

what: Keep 3 copies of important files, on 2 different types of storage (e.g., laptop drive and cloud), with 1 copy off-site; make backups automatic and test a restore; organise files in a simple folder structure (e.g., Personal / Portfolio / Study / Documents).
dose: 3 copies, 2 media types, 1 off-site (CISA); frequency: 'automatically and regularly'
why: CISA recommends the 3-2-1 rule, automatic regular backups, offline copies and tested restores to protect against data loss and ransomware.

sources.title: CISA - Back Up Government Data (3-2-1 rule)

cue_suggestion: First day of month: check backup status
minimum_version: Turn on automatic cloud backup for phone photos and Documents.
normal_version: Add an external drive backup; monthly check that backups ran.
bonus_version: Quarterly: restore one file to test; tidy Downloads into the folder structure.
joy_pairing: Peace of mind for the portfolio: pair with an archive moment (export your latest work files).
friction_down: Automatic backup settings; drive kept next to the laptop charger.
if_then_plan: If it is the first day of the month, then I will check the backup date and plug in the external drive.
safety_or_stop_rule: Encrypt backups holding documents/ID scans; keep one copy offline.

what: Turn on 2-step verification (MFA) on email first, then banking, Absher, social media, shopping, cloud storage and the password manager; prefer an authenticator app or passkey where offered.
dose: One-off setup per account
why: NCSC calls turning on 2SV the first and most important step to protect you if your password gets phished; CISA advises enabling MFA on email, banks and other important accounts.

sources.title: NCSC - Top tips for staying secure online: Password managers
CISA Secure Our World - Turn On MFA

cue_suggestion: Life-admin block; one account per week
normal_version: Email + bank + Absher + main social account.
bonus_version: All accounts in the password manager; store backup codes securely.
joy_pairing: Security 'score' in the app filling up.
friction_down: Follow Settings > Security > 2-step; install one authenticator app.
if_then_plan: If an account shows 'turn on 2-step verification', then I will do it immediately.
safety_or_stop_rule: Save recovery/backup codes offline; never share one-time codes with anyone (including callers claiming to be a bank or government).

what: Use a password manager to generate strong, unique passwords per account; give email a strong separate password; protect the manager with 2SV.
dose: One-off setup, then as-needed
why: NCSC: password managers create strong unique passwords, autofill, sync across devices and alert on breaches.

sources.title: NCSC - Top tips for staying secure online: Password managers

cue_suggestion: Whenever you log in to an account not yet in the manager

name_en: Weekly partial water change + gravel clean

what: Replace part of the tank water each week and vacuum the gravel to remove waste; use dechlorinated water at tank temperature.
dose: 10-25% of tank water weekly (RSPCA, tropical fish)
why: Regular partial water changes with gravel cleaning keep water quality safe for fish.

safety_or_stop_rule: If fish gasp at the surface or look ill, test water and seek advice from an aquatic vet/specialist.

name_en: Feed small amounts at fixed times
name_ar: إطعام كميات صغيرة في أوقات ثابتة
what: Feed only what fish eat within a couple of minutes, at consistent times; remove uneaten food.
dose: Sources differ: RSPCA Australia (tropical) once a day, what is eaten in under 2 minutes; RSPCA UK two or three times a day, what is eaten in 2-5 minutes. Follow advice for your species.
why: Overfeeding degrades water quality, and fish are more susceptible to poor water than to a lack of food.

name_en: Test water and rinse filter in tank water
name_ar: فحص الماء وشطف الفلتر بماء الحوض
what: Test ammonia and nitrite; rinse the filter media lightly in a bucket of tank water (not tap water) when clogged or monthly.
dose: Test every 2-3 days for the first 6 weeks, then every 1-2 weeks; filter rinse monthly or when clogged, whichever first (RSPCA Australia)
why: Monitoring and gentle filter maintenance protect water quality.

what: Language and flows distinguish a lapse (a slip) from a relapse (return to the old pattern).
